Alex — thanks, this is great. Quick answers up front and a proposed plan attached.

Short answers:
- ACLs/ports: We only require outbound TLS (443) from the private hosts to our control endpoints and inbound application ports to the LB from your transit network. Detailed matrix is in the attached network-physical-mapping.vsdx (page 2).
- Management plane: No permanent inbound from your management plane is required. For the activation window we ask for ephemeral SSH access to the bastion (audit logged) — see step 1.2 in the runbook.
- Priming: Yes — we recommend pre-staging a 15-min synthetic traffic mirror at 2 rps per shard to warm KV caches, then ramp to 20 rps during the sanity-swarm.

Proposed window and owners (20 May):
- 09:00–09:30 PDT — pre-check: network connectivity, NTP, certs (Owner: Laura Bennett)
- 09:30–10:15 PDT — kv warmup & prefix prime (Owner: Mateo Alvarez)
- 10:15–11:00 PDT — sanity-swarm (functional smoke): generation, streaming, and fallback validation (Owner: Neha Kapoor)
- 11:00–11:30 PDT — runbook handback and metrics review (Owner: Vivek Kulkarni)

I've attached a compact runbook and a short checklist for the ops team. Please review the network diagram and the kv-warmup-checklist.csv and confirm whether ephemeral bastion creds can be provisioned for 20 May 08:50 PDT.

Attachments: redwood_runbook_v2.pdf, network-physical-mapping.vsdx, kv-warmup-checklist.csv

Best,
Neha Kapoor

Quick tech notes / additions to Neha's plan: 
- Network: Confirm MTU across the transit path is >= 9000 if you plan jumbo frames. We saw tail drops in a lab when PMTU was mismatched (linked doc in Drive).
- Bastion: We'll create a one-time SSH cert valid 30 minutes either side of the window; ops, please provide the public key for logging.
- KV warmup: Mateo, please ensure the cache-priming job pins prefixes to node groups A/B to validate cache affinity. See attached kv-warmup-checklist.csv for exact curl sequences.

Also adding a quick rollback trigger: if rate of 5xx > 1% for a sustained 3 minutes during the sanity-swarm, automatic route fallback will send traffic to the hosted fallback pool. Ops — is that acceptable?

-Vivek
